behaviors.behavior: A dismiss recorded only in a worktree's tracked log resolves as dismissed on main, not still-open triage
Once the deciding event reaches main's own tracked log, the item reads plain dismissed with no pending marker
The pending-delivery envelope names the branch holding an undelivered decision
A status decision and an amend for the same id on two DIFFERENT branches are attributed to their own branch, never collapsed into one
behaviors.evidence: test_build_listing_keeps_status_and_amend_branches_separate PASSED (Stage-3 doubt review finding 2, empirically reconstructed)

behaviors.behavior: A foreign append never seeds an item this tree never created itself (only KNOWN ids fold in)
A tie between a foreign and a local event of identical timestamp is broken by file-order, not physical origin
Sibling-worktree discovery finds a branch and its tracked log; is empty from inside a worktree, with no .worktrees dir, or for a detached HEAD
A relative gitdir: target (git >= 2.48) resolves against the worktree's own directory, not the process CWD
Only status/amend events ever reach a caller from a foreign log; a foreign append's body is filtered out before caching
The (path, mtime) discovery and per-file caches take their cache-hit branch on a second call with no filesystem change, and invalidate when a sibling is added
Every unreadable/malformed worktree shape (a directory where .git should be a file, a gitdir: line missing, an admin dir with no HEAD, .worktrees existing as a file) is skipped, never crashes
cross_tree_delivery_facts returns two separate branch maps end-to-end (status, amend), and returns empty at no cost on a tree with no siblings
foreign_undelivered_from_records rejects an empty applied_statuses vocabulary rather than silently reporting nothing as pending
The human pending-delivery notice labels an id with a known origin branch differently from one without
build_listing's new origin_branches parameters are optional — every existing call site keeps working unchanged
